title: I made a cyberpunk roguelike RPG with AI, and I'd love a few people to try it
author: Poli_1983
selftext:
Hi everyone.

First, a disclaimer: I'm Italian, and English isn't my first language. I've done my best with this post, but some of it will probably read a bit off. Sorry in advance.

**Neon Echoes: The Hollow Shell** is a text-driven roguelike RPG for Android in pixel art style with a Blade Runner like visual reference.

You wake up in a body that isn't yours, with no memory. You investigate a murder in your  
own way. Every completed run may generates a different culprit and in a roguelike way you unlock what you learn for the next run.

Here are some features:

* **True roguelike:** every run start from scratch. The only things unlocked is what you learn
* **Quick games:** a run doesn't take time more than 30-45 minutes if you achieve an ending
* **Tag system:** what you choose records what you can enabled to see during your run
* **Trait and moral quadrant:** your choices and your behaviour will plasm your run

It's openly inspired from three things I love:

* **Disco Elysium** — for character handling and inventory management. Your stats are your personality, and they decide which choices you're even allowed to see.
* **Reigns** — for resource management. Any of them hitting zero ends the run, each in its own way.
* **Life at Adventure** — for the plot structure. A main investigation threaded through random events and mini-quests.

There is no combat (for the moment?) It's all dialogue, D20 skill checks and consequences.

Is developed with Godot 4.7 and supports two languages: English and Italian.

21 possible culprits combination, 7 main endings plus mini-quest endings.

*Here comes the honest part*

**This game was built almost entirely with AI.** Code, pixel art (some AI, some are public assets), text, icons:

I directed it, argued with it, and rewrote a lot of what it produced, but I'm not going to pretend otherwise. If that's a dealbreaker for you, I completely understand, and thanks for reading this far.

**I have no idea what I'm doing on mobile.** This is my first Android project. I've learned what an AAB is, what a keystore is, and why Godot resolves relative export paths against the project directory (that one cost me an afternoon), all in the last few weeks. There will be things that are obviously wrong to anyone experienced. I'd genuinely like to hear about them.

**My goal is small.** I want it on the Play Store, and I'd like to find one person who actually enjoys playing it. That would be enough. I'm not chasing downloads or revenue (ok honestly some ads and microtransactions just for checking if developing games can be economically valuable for a bunch of dollars).

**If you'd like to have a look:**

It's in closed testing on Play, so access works in two steps:

1. Join the group (Play only grants access to emails on this list - I hope i did anything right for giving access 😄 ):   [https://groups.google.com/g/neonechoestester](https://groups.google.com/g/neonechoestester)

2. Open the test link with the same Google account:   [https://play.google.com/apps/internaltest/4701710406476164446](https://play.google.com/apps/internaltest/4701710406476164446)

If something breaks or you have an idea, the tracker is here:  
[https://github.com/pamontag-org-ghe/neonechoes-thehollowshell-public](https://github.com/pamontag-org-ghe/neonechoes-thehollowshell-public)

No pressure and no obligation: installing it and poking around for five minutes

Is already more than I expected when I started this. 

**Thanks really in advance for reading.** **Every suggestion will be helpful.**
